name: 88Sr+ loading by laser ablation and Doppler cooling in a surface-electrode RF ion trap at about 6 K and 1e-8 torr
plain_name: Trap and laser-cool single charged atoms above a chip in a cold vacuum
description: Mount a silver-on-sapphire surface-electrode trap (five DC control electrodes, two RF electrodes, 200 V at 18.45 MHz) on the 4 K stage of a bath or low-vibration closed-cycle cryostat, reach about 1e-8 torr by cryopumping, load 88Sr+ by laser ablation and Doppler-cool with 422 nm and 1091 nm lasers through side windows while imaging through a bottom window.
keywords: Trap and laser-cool single charged atoms above a chip in a cold vacuum

sources.citation: Cryogenic Ion Trapping Systems with Surface-Electrode Traps (Antohi et al., arXiv:0807.4763; Rev. Sci. Instrum. 80, 013103, 2009)

reported_equipment: Advanced Research Systems (Model GMX-20B) low vibration cryostat
surface-electrode ion trap (silver thin film on sapphire)

requirements.rationale: The trap ran at 6.0 K with 200 V RF applied; the cold stage must hold the trap at about 6 K.
Ion trapping needs an evacuated (UHV) sample space.
Long trapped-ion lifetimes required a working pressure of 1e-8 torr (the closed-cycle version reached 3e-9 torr at the ion pump).
Ablation, 422 nm cooling, 1091 nm repumping and ion imaging all need windows to the trap.
Each of the five DC control electrodes must be wired out (the paper uses two wires per electrode).
RF (200 V, 18.45 MHz) and DC voltages must reach the trap electrodes.
Optional: the closed-cycle variant was qualified with cold-tip displacement below 106 nm.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
